validity_findings.observation: Frozen spec and implementation define encoding_agnostic_decode as iterative try brotli->gzip->identity until SHA256 matches ground truth (spec.json measurement_validity #3, prereg.md section 7 algorithm, run_experiment.py:218 encoding_agnostic_decode with ground_truth_sha256 arg). This is correct for testing whether CDN transforms are lossless but is circular as a product mechanism: success is defined as matching the oracle SHA, so 240/240 is tautologically achievable if any decompression chain yields that SHA and formats are distinguishable. Deployable decoder cannot use ground truth.
validity_findings.impact: Inflates product readiness claim; does not invalidate lossless-recovery observation but requires oracle-free validation before promotion

claim_ceiling: MAXIMUM JUSTIFIED: Encoding-agnostic ORACLE-guided iterative decompression (try brotli then gzip iteratively until SHA256 equals within-run ground truth) losslessly recovers the ground-truth bytes for all tested transformations applied by Cloudflare free-tier quick tunnel (edge iad05, DYNAMIC only, no HIT observed) on 10KB nominal payloads (JSON 5.57, HTML 4.66, BINARY 7.69 bits/byte) and 150KB large payloads, across 48 primary cells (3 payload types x 2 stacking orders x 2 client chunk sizes x 4 Accept-Encoding variants, N=5 per cell, unique URLs, jitter 200-500ms) and generalizes to depths 3-5 alternating brotli(q4)/gzip(L1) stacking and to 150KB payloads (100% on deduped 45 depth + 30 large observations). Positive control 240/240 localhost and null control 15/15 identity pass; fixed-order regression 60/240 replicates parent. NOT JUSTIFIED: Deployable oracle-free decompression without ground truth (products cannot use SHA oracle); CDN HIT/stale-cache behavior (0 HIT observed); other CDN providers/tiers/edges; concurrent load; HTTP/2 or H3 framing; mixed chunk-size pipelines; paid-tier or globally distributed edge behavior. Product Core promotion requires: (a) demonstration that greedy oracle-free iteration (try brotli/gzip until failure) yields 240/240 without SHA check on same matrix, stored with byte-level recomputable artifact, plus HIT staleness test.

unresolved: Does oracle-free greedy iterative decompression (no SHA check) achieve 240/240 on same 48 CDN cells? Spec requires ground truth to declare success; deployable kernel cannot use it. Greedy likely succeeds given distinct gzip/brotli headers but not measured here and not independently recomputable without raw bytes.
Does encoding-agnostic decode recover correctness for CDN HIT (stale) responses? All 423 CDN responses are DYNAMIC; HIT path not exercised despite fixed-URL cache stability design.

Does effect generalize to other CDN providers (Fastly, Akamai, CloudFront), paid tiers, other geographic edges, HTTP/2 or H3, concurrent clients, or mixed chunk-size pipelines? Explicitly not tested per report section 6.
What is amortized latency/cost of iterative try-brotli-then-gzip versus fixed-order decode? Not measured.

Were depth 3-5 and large-payload CDN deliveries also DYNAMIC and under same Accept-Encoding both condition (true per deduped rows) — does CDN re-encoding at deeper depths ever produce ambiguous bytes where both brotli and gzip decompress successfully (oracle tie-break needed)? Not observed but not falsified at deeper depths with other quality/level settings.
